# zhbtrd

> Reduces a complex Hermitian band matrix to real tridiagonal form by unitary similarity transformation.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zhbtrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhbtrd';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zhbtrd(
    order,
    vect, uplo,
    N, kd,
    AB, LDAB,
    d, strideD,
    e, strideE,
    Q, LDQ,
    WORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `vect` | `("none"\|"initialize"\|"update")` | in |  | one of `'none'`, `'update'`, `'initialize'` | `'none'`, `'initialize'`, or `'update'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kd ≥ 0` | number of super- (or sub-) diagonals |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `kd + 1 × N` |  | band matrix (LDAB x N) |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kd + 1`; row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `AB` |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for diagonal elements (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array` | out | `N - 1` |  | output array for off-diagonal elements (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `e` |
| `Q` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | unitary matrix (LDQ x N) |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldq < max( 1, N ) && (vect === 'initialize' \|\| vect === 'update')` | leading dimension of `Q` |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | workspace (length N) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `vect`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not form Q;
  -   `= 'V'`: form Q;
  -   `= 'U'`: update a matrix X, by forming $X \, Q$.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$. On exit, the diagonal elements of `AB` are overwritten by the diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T; if $\mathrm{KD} > 0$, the elements on the first superdiagonal (if `UPLO = 'U'`) or the first subdiagonal (if `UPLO = 'L'`) are overwritten by the off-diagonal elements of T; the rest of `AB` is overwritten by values generated during the reduction.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `e`: The off-diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T: $E(i) = T(i,i+1)$ if `UPLO = 'U'`; $E(i) = T(i+1,i)$ if `UPLO = 'L'`.
- `Q`: On entry, if `VECT = 'U'`, then Q must contain an N-by-N matrix X; if `VECT = 'N'` or 'V', then Q need not be set.

  On exit: if `VECT = 'V'`, Q contains the N-by-N unitary matrix Q; if `VECT = 'U'`, Q contains the product $X \, Q$; if `VECT = 'N'`, the array Q is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "none", "update", "initialize"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDQ < max( 1, N ) && ( vect === "initialize" \|\| vect === "update" )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zhbtrd.ndarray(
    vect, uplo,
    N, kd,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vect` | `("none"\|"initialize"\|"update")` | in |  | one of `'none'`, `'update'`, `'initialize'` | specifies the operation type |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | specifies the operation type |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kd ≥ 0` | the number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `uplo === 'upper'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `uplo === 'lower'`. |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `kd + 1 × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AB` |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array` | out | `N - 1` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `e` |
| `Q` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `Q` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |

<details>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. </details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "none", "update", "initialize"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import zhbtrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhbtrd';

// 4x4 Hermitian tridiagonal (KD=1), upper band storage (LDAB=2):

const AB = new Complex128Array( 8 );
AB.set( [ 4, 0 ], 1 );
AB.set( [ 1, 1 ], 2 );
AB.set( [ 5, 0 ], 3 );
AB.set( [ 2, -1 ], 4 );
AB.set( [ 6, 0 ], 5 );
AB.set( [ 3, 1 ], 6 );
AB.set( [ 7, 0 ], 7 );
const d = new Float64Array( 4 );
const e = new Float64Array( 3 );
const Q = new Complex128Array( 16 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 4 );

zhbtrd( 'column-major', 'initialize', 'upper', 4, 1, AB, 2, d, 1, e, 1, Q, 4, WORK );

console.log( 'Diagonal (d):', d ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Off-diagonal (e):', e ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZHBTRD`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZHBTRD reduces a complex Hermitian band matrix A to real symmetric tridiagonal form T by a unitary similarity transformation: $Q^H \, A \, Q = T$.

### Further Details

Modified by Linda Kaufman, Bell Labs.

</section>
